We're looking for a Subject Matter Expert (SME) to lead our Dutch audio transcription project. Belgium's rich Dutch-language community — particularly across Flanders — makes it an ideal base for this role. Your familiarity with Flemish speech patterns, regional accents, and the nuances that distinguish Belgian Dutch from its northern counterpart will be a genuine asset.

This is a hands-on leadership role that rewards sound judgment, clear communication, and a sharp ear for language. You'll guide a team through the natural messiness of real-world audio while keeping quality standards high and the team aligned.

Experience with audio transcription, data labeling, linguistic annotation, quality assurance, or AI/ML data projects preferred

Excellent written and verbal communication skills in Dutch
Experience providing feedback, coaching, or leading teams is preferred
Comfortable working independently and managing multiple project priorities
Familiarity with Discord or similar online collaboration platforms

Knowledge of Flemish regional accents — from Ghent and Antwerp to West Flanders

jobs.description:
Job Description

Job Function Summary

Involves gathering, analyzing, and interpreting a wide variety of research data. Designs and conducts research including selecting data samples, developing research instruments, analyzing collected information according to established statistical methods, and developing recommendations based on research findings. Prepares reports, charts, tables, and other visual aids to interpret and communicate data and results.

Generic Scope

Professional who applies acquired job skills, policies, and procedures to complete substantive assignments / projects / tasks of moderate scope and complexity; exercises judgment within defined guidelines and practices to determine appropriate action.

Custom Scope

This is a part-time (50% FTE) Research Data Analyst position supporting two investigators conducting research on substance use, addiction, and harm reduction services across diverse clinical and community settings. The analyst will contribute to multiple research projects, with a primary focus on data management, statistical analysis, interpretation, and visualization.

The ideal candidate will have training or experience in epidemiology, public health, biostatistics, or a related field, and mixed-methods research skills. Experience working with both large and small datasets, including data cleaning, preparation, management, sycronization, and statistical analysis, is required. Proficiency in R is strongly preferred, particularly for statistical analysis and data visualization, and experience with ArcGIS is desirable. Knowledge of or experience working with harm reduction programs, substance use treatment settings, low-barrier clinics, or populations affected by substance use is preferred. The successful candidate should be comfortable working collaboratively across multiple projects and investigators and translating analytic findings into clear tables, figures, presentations, and manuscripts.

Department Overview

The Division of Prevention Science is a leading force in prevention research innovation. We conduct transformative research, bridging communities and overcoming health inequities through high-impact prevention. The division was established within the Department of Medicine in 1991 and is the administrative home of the Center for AIDS Prevention Studies (CAPS), and the Prevention Research Center (PRC). The division is committed to advancing knowledge in prevention and has extensive expertise in social and behavioral research applied to prevention science and the development of effective prevention interventions across several disease domains. The research focus is risk behavior and reduction; epidemiology of the virus; evaluation of HIV testing procedures, demographic variables and sexual self-identification; and training for providers who care for HIV AIDS patients. While much of the work in DPS has traditionally focused on HIV/AIDS, many investigators are doing important work in other fields including cardiovascular disease, cancer, mental health, and substance abuse. The Division is composed of approximately 35 academics (faculty, fellows and specialists) and 45 non-academic staff who come from a variety of social, behavioral and policy science academic disciplines, including psychology, sociology, anthropology, epidemiology, history, political science, economics, demography, nursing, pharmacy and statistics.

The Division is home to three federally funded research centers that provide valuable infrastructure support: 1) The Center for AIDS Prevention Studies, funded by the National Institute of Mental Health; 2) The UCSF Prevention Research Center, funded by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention; 3) three evaluation centers funded by the Health Resources and Services Administration; and 4) a newly-funded research coordinating center to reduce disparities in multiple chronic diseases, funded by the National Institute on Minority Health and Health Disparities. The Division is also home to the Center of Excellence for Transgender Health and over 100 active sponsored research projects.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Experience conducting epidemiological studies using large and small datasets, and working knowledge of research function.
Working skills in statistical analysis, systems programming, database design and data security measures.
Experience in data management and analysis using R and geospatial analysis using ArcGIS software programs.
Communicates complex information in a clear and concise manner both verbally and in writing.
At least one year of experience working with harm reduction organizations, treatment center or low barrier clinics that serve people with a substance use disorder.

Preferred Qualifications

Working skills in conducting interviews and administering surveys (data collection).
Experience working on mixed methods studies that integrates qualitative and quantitative datasets.

Required Education

Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training.

Preferred Education

Master’s degree in biostatistics, epidemiology or another closely related field.

Licenses

None listed.

Certifications

None listed.

jobs.description:
PsiQuantum's mission is to build the first useful quantum computers: machines capable of delivering the breakthroughs the field has long promised. Since our founding in 2016, our singular focus has been to build and deploy million-qubit, fault-tolerant quantum systems.

Quantum computers harness the laws of quantum mechanics to solve problems that even the most advanced supercomputers or AI systems will never reach. Their impact will span energy, pharmaceuticals, finance, agriculture, transportation, materials, and other foundational industries.

Our architecture and approach is based on silicon photonics. By leveraging the advanced semiconductor manufacturing industry, including partners like GlobalFoundries, we use the same high-volume processes that already produce billions of chips for telecom and consumer electronics. Photonics offers natural advantages for scale: photons don't feel heat, are immune to electromagnetic interference, and integrate with existing cryogenic cooling and standard fiber-optic infrastructure.

That approach has since been tested at the highest level of scrutiny the U.S. government applies to emerging technology, and it has held up. In 2025, PsiQuantum closed a $1 billion funding round that valued the company at $7 billion. In 2026, the U.S. Department of Commerce signed a $100 million Letter of Intent under the CHIPS and Science Act, followed by a $125 million agreement with DARPA under Stage C of its Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, PsiQuantum's most valuable U.S. government agreement to date. This year, we also broke ground on our utility-scale quantum computer in Brisbane, Australia, and continued building out our Chicago site. Victor Peng, our CEO, and co-founder Jeremy O'Brien, now Executive Chairman, lead a team and board that reflects how seriously the world is taking this build, joined this year by Intel's Lip-Bu Tan and Atomico's Niklas Zennström.

PsiQuantum also develops the algorithms and software needed to make these systems commercially valuable. Our application, software, and industry teams work directly with leading Fortune 500 companies, including Airbus, Lockheed Martin, Mercedes-Benz, Boehringer Ingelheim, and Mitsubishi Chemical, to prepare quantum solutions for real-world impact.

Quantum computing is not an extension of classical computing. It represents a fundamental shift, and a path to mastering challenges that cannot be solved any other way. who is ready to bring their expertise to a high-impact environment and help us build a brand-new category of technology.

About The Role

In this role you will perform, analyze, and interpret the characterization of our nanoelectronic semiconductor devices at various stages of their lifecycle. Such characterization makes up a crucial part of our quality control process to ensure received devices meet the required specifications and also provides crucial feedback following experimentation as part of our test and learning cycles. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in Physics, Materials Science and or Nanotechnology, be rigorous and detail oriented, work well within a highly interdisciplinary environment and be eager to learn and contribute.

Responsibilities

Perform characterization of devices using a wide range of metrology techniques including atomic force microscopy (AFM), photoinduced force microscopy (PiFM), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and nanoelectronic measurements.
Work closely with outside vendors, collaborators, and fabrication partners to coordinate the characterization of devices using techniques such as time-of-flight mass spectroscopy (TOF-SIM/nano-SIMs), x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR).
Prepare reports on pristine (as received) nanoelectronic devices using the techniques listed above as part of our standard quality control processes.
Prepare experimental summaries characterizing devices after various experiments to provide feedback as part of our test and learning cycles.
Understand the requirements of our nanoelectronic devices and propose characterization techniques to ensure devices meet these specifications.
Maintain detailed and meticulous records of all experimental work and analysis.
Effectively communicate experimental results, data analysis, and next steps with our chip fabrication, device measurements, surface chemistry teams, and the wider company.

Job Description

The Quality Control Technician for battery materials is responsible for screening, characterizing, and performing quality control on raw materials that support electrode and cell development programs. In this role, you operate a suite of analytical instruments to generate high-quality materials data that directly informs purchasing decisions, supplier qualification, and formulation development. This position suits someone who enjoys detailed, measurement-intensive work, takes pride in producing reliable analytical data, and helps keep materials programs running smoothly.

Responsibilities

Perform incoming materials characterization on raw materials and make clear pass or fail determinations against established acceptance criteria.
Operate analytical instruments for materials characterization, including particle size analyzers, BET surface area analyzers, X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive spectroscopy (SEM/EDS), thermal analysis instruments such as TGA and DSC, slurry rheology equipment, and conductivity measurement tools.
Carry out wet chemistry sample preparation and analysis, including titration and related techniques, to support materials characterization.
Prepare materials samples using techniques such as milling, drying, pressing, and cross-sectioning to ensure consistent and reliable analysis.
Maintain and update the materials inventory database, ensuring accurate tracking of raw materials and test results.
Support supplier qualification by generating comparative characterization datasets across different vendor samples and summarizing findings.
Generate clear characterization reports, data summaries, and tables that communicate results to internal stakeholders.
Escalate anomalous results, unexpected trends, or potential instrument performance issues promptly to ensure timely investigation and resolution.
Perform routine instrument maintenance, calibration, and troubleshooting on analytical equipment to ensure consistent and accurate performance.
Maintain calibration logs, standard reference trackers, and standard operating procedure (SOP) documentation, and coordinate service calls with external providers as needed.
Follow all chemical hygiene, personal protective equipment (PPE), and safety protocols while working with materials and analytical instruments.
Manage consumables inventory, including chemicals, standards, and lab supplies, to support uninterrupted laboratory operations.
Keep characterization laboratory spaces clean, organized, and compliant with safety and quality standards.
Contribute to the writing, review, and updating of SOPs to reflect best practices and continuous improvement in laboratory processes.

Essential Skills

13 years of hands-on experience operating analytical instruments in a materials, chemistry, or battery laboratory environment; internship experience counts toward this requirement.
Strong background in chemistry or analytical chemistry, with practical laboratory experience.
Proficiency with materials characterization techniques such as particle size analysis, BET surface area analysis, X-ray diffraction (XRD), SEM/EDS, thermal analysis (TGA/DSC), and rheometry or slurry rheology.
Experience with materials sample preparation techniques, including milling, drying, pressing, and cross-sectioning.
High attention to detail and a methodical approach to measurement and data collection.
Demonstrated commitment to data quality, including careful documentation, verification, and review of results.
Ability to read, interpret, and implement standard operating procedures (SOPs) accurately.
Capability to contribute to the drafting and updating of SOPs based on laboratory experience and process improvements.
Knowledge of laboratory safety practices, including safe chemical handling, PPE requirements, and emergency procedures.
Ability to operate and maintain analytical instruments, perform routine calibrations, and troubleshoot basic equipment issues.
Strong organizational skills for maintaining inventory databases, calibration logs, and laboratory documentation.

Additional Skills & Qualifications

Academic or practical training in materials science, chemistry, chemical engineering, or a related discipline.
Experience working in a battery, energy storage, or advanced materials laboratory environment.
Familiarity with generating comparative datasets to support supplier qualification and material selection.
Experience writing clear technical reports, summary tables, and documentation for internal stakeholders.
Comfort working in a fast-paced, data-driven environment where analytical results inform purchasing and development decisions.

This role is fully onsite in a laboratory environment in San Leandro. Job Title: Quality Control Lab Technician

Job Description

The Quality Control Lab Technician supports a high-volume manufacturing operation by performing accurate and timely quality testing on raw materials, bulk batches, and finished products. This role ensures that products meet strict specifications, communicates test results and batch adjustments clearly to production operators, and initiates investigations into non-conforming materials. The position offers strong long-term growth potential for someone who is proactive, detail-oriented, and eager to streamline testing processes and advance into higher-level technical roles over time.

Schedule: Thursday- Monday or Friday-Tuesday (8 am - 5 pm) or (7 am-4 pm)

Responsibilities

Execute and adhere to all environmental, health, and safety (EHS) requirements, maintaining a safe work environment and following internal safety rules and procedures, including wearing appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE).
Participate in the general housekeeping of the plant and laboratory areas to maintain a clean, organized, and compliant workspace.
Comply with all company policies, procedures, and quality standards in daily activities.
Perform timely and accurate chemical, physical, and visual testing on raw materials, bulk batches, and finished goods using standard test procedures.
Determine raw material adjustment amounts for bulk batches to ensure products meet required specifications.
Enter test results for raw materials, bulk batches, and finished goods into the ERP system (SAP) accurately and promptly.
Perform timely usage decisions (accept or reject) for raw materials, bulk batches, and finished goods in SAP based on test results and specifications.
Collect and store retain samples of raw materials, bulk batches, and finished products as required for traceability and future investigations.
Take immediate action on internal non-conformances by creating notifications in SAP and performing initial investigations in collaboration with production operators.
Support customer complaint investigations by reviewing batch records, analyzing retain samples, and contributing to root cause analysis and corrective actions.
Maintain critical laboratory equipment, including routine checks and basic troubleshooting, to support continuous and uninterrupted quality control testing.
Monitor and maintain laboratory inventory of reagents, consumables, and supplies to ensure consistent testing capability.
Review the daily production schedule and ensure that test equipment, reagents, and methods are prepared to efficiently test all scheduled batches.
Provide accurate documentation and visual quality control labels for materials and products that are acceptable, rejected, or on hold.
Issue, complete, maintain, and process all relevant paperwork and records related to testing, non-conformances, and quality documentation.
Participate in monthly meetings focused on quality, safety, housekeeping, and waste minimization, contributing ideas for continuous improvement.
Communicate all critical issues and problems concerning quality control test equipment, potential testing delays, and quality risks promptly to management.
Act as a proactive team player by volunteering to help where needed, supporting colleagues, and contributing to shared goals.
Apply lean manufacturing and continuous improvement principles, including participation in audits, root cause and corrective action activities, and documentation updates.
Manage multiple testing tasks and projects concurrently, demonstrating strong time management and prioritization skills in a laboratory setting.
Serve as a reliable gatekeeper for production quality by responding quickly to issues, ensuring that non-conforming material is identified and addressed immediately.

Essential Skills

Bachelor of Science degree in Chemical Engineering or Chemistry.
Minimum of 1+ years of experience, which may include internships or early-career roles, preferably in aerospace, manufacturing, or consumer products environments.
Hands-on experience performing chemical, physical, and visual testing in a laboratory or production support setting.
Proficiency with ERP systems, specifically SAP, including entering test results and making usage decisions.
Working knowledge of Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Teams, and Microsoft Outlook for data management, communication, and coordination.
Strong communication skills with the ability to communicate promptly and clearly, and to be proactive rather than reactive.
High attention to detail and accuracy in testing, documentation, and data entry.
Experience participating in audits and working within ISO or similar quality management environments.
Exposure to or experience with root cause analysis and corrective action processes, including updating documentation.
Familiarity with lean manufacturing concepts and continuous improvement practices.
Ability to manage time effectively and handle multiple tasks in a fast-paced lab and production environment.
Demonstrated ability to work both independently and under the direction of senior lab staff, such as senior lab technicians, lab supervisors, or technical leaders.
Strong sense of ownership and responsibility as a quality gatekeeper for production.

Additional Skills & Qualifications

Experience in aerospace, manufacturing, or consumer products industries, particularly in operations or production support roles.
Familiarity with GC-MS (Gas ChromatographyMass Spectrometry) or similar analytical instrumentation.
Exposure to Six Sigma or other structured problem-solving methodologies.
Experience working in a quality control laboratory that supports adhesives or chemical products.
Prior involvement in customer complaint investigations and non-conformance management.
Experience working in a lean manufacturing environment with a focus on waste minimization and process optimization.
Demonstrated ability to streamline testing processes and reduce redundancy in lab workflows.
Proven record of participating in continuous improvement initiatives, including documentation updates and process enhancements.
Strong professional attitude with a desire to learn, grow, and assume greater responsibility over time, including potential progression into senior or leadership roles.
Willingness to consider future relocation for long-term career growth opportunities.

The environment emphasizes project and time management, lean manufacturing, and continuous improvement, with regular participation in quality, safety, housekeeping, and waste minimization meetings. The culture values proactive communication, teamwork, and professional growth, offering long-term development opportunities for individuals who are motivated, adaptable, and eager to take on increasing responsibility.

Job Description

This role focuses on logging, tracking, and coordinating the receipt and shipment of samples into and out of the laboratory while ensuring accurate documentation and regulatory compliance. Log and track the receipt and shipment of all samples into and out of the laboratory while verifying receipt of samples.

Maintain and promote safety at all times by conducting all operations in a safe and environmentally compliant manner.

Strong verbal and written communication skills to interact clearly with internal teams and accurately document sample information.

57 years of experience in a laboratory, sample control, or closely related environment.

Experience working with Laboratory Management Systems for logging and tracking samples.

Department Overview

The Division of Prevention Science is a leading force in prevention research innovation. We conduct transformative research, bridging communities and overcoming health inequities through high-impact prevention. The division was established within the Department of Medicine in 1991 and is the administrative home of the Center for AIDS Prevention Studies (CAPS), and the Prevention Research Center (PRC). The division is committed to advancing knowledge in prevention and has extensive expertise in social and behavioral research applied to prevention science and the development of effective prevention interventions across several disease domains. The research focus is risk behavior and reduction; epidemiology of the virus; evaluation of HIV testing procedures, demographic variables and sexual self-identification; and training for providers who care for HIV AIDS patients. While much of the work in DPS has traditionally focused on HIV/AIDS, many investigators are doing important work in other fields including cardiovascular disease, cancer, mental health, and substance abuse. The Division is composed of approximately 35 academics (faculty, fellows and specialists) and 45 non-academic staff who come from a variety of social, behavioral and policy science academic disciplines, including psychology, sociology, anthropology, epidemiology, history, political science, economics, demography, nursing, pharmacy and statistics.

The Division is home to three federally funded research centers that provide valuable infrastructure support: 1) The Center for AIDS Prevention Studies, funded by the National Institute of Mental Health; 2) The UCSF Prevention Research Center, funded by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention; 3) three evaluation centers funded by the Health Resources and Services Administration; and 4) a newly-funded research coordinating center to reduce disparities in multiple chronic diseases, funded by the National Institute on Minority Health and Health Disparities. The Division is also home to the Center of Excellence for Transgender Health and over 100 active sponsored research projects.

Working skills in conducting interviews and administering surveys (data collection).
Experience working on mixed methods studies that integrates qualitative and quantitative datasets.

Job Description

The Quality Control Technician for battery materials is responsible for screening, characterizing, and performing quality control on raw materials that support electrode and cell development programs. In this role, you operate a suite of analytical instruments to generate high-quality materials data that directly informs purchasing decisions, supplier qualification, and formulation development. This position suits someone who enjoys detailed, measurement-intensive work, takes pride in producing reliable analytical data, and helps keep materials programs running smoothly.

Responsibilities

Perform incoming materials characterization on raw materials and make clear pass or fail determinations against established acceptance criteria.
Operate analytical instruments for materials characterization, including particle size analyzers, BET surface area analyzers, X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive spectroscopy (SEM/EDS), thermal analysis instruments such as TGA and DSC, slurry rheology equipment, and conductivity measurement tools.
Carry out wet chemistry sample preparation and analysis, including titration and related techniques, to support materials characterization.
Prepare materials samples using techniques such as milling, drying, pressing, and cross-sectioning to ensure consistent and reliable analysis.
Maintain and update the materials inventory database, ensuring accurate tracking of raw materials and test results.
Support supplier qualification by generating comparative characterization datasets across different vendor samples and summarizing findings.
Generate clear characterization reports, data summaries, and tables that communicate results to internal stakeholders.
Escalate anomalous results, unexpected trends, or potential instrument performance issues promptly to ensure timely investigation and resolution.
Perform routine instrument maintenance, calibration, and troubleshooting on analytical equipment to ensure consistent and accurate performance.
Maintain calibration logs, standard reference trackers, and standard operating procedure (SOP) documentation, and coordinate service calls with external providers as needed.
Follow all chemical hygiene, personal protective equipment (PPE), and safety protocols while working with materials and analytical instruments.
Manage consumables inventory, including chemicals, standards, and lab supplies, to support uninterrupted laboratory operations.
Keep characterization laboratory spaces clean, organized, and compliant with safety and quality standards.
Contribute to the writing, review, and updating of SOPs to reflect best practices and continuous improvement in laboratory processes.

Essential Skills

13 years of hands-on experience operating analytical instruments in a materials, chemistry, or battery laboratory environment; internship experience counts toward this requirement.
Strong background in chemistry or analytical chemistry, with practical laboratory experience.
Proficiency with materials characterization techniques such as particle size analysis, BET surface area analysis, X-ray diffraction (XRD), SEM/EDS, thermal analysis (TGA/DSC), and rheometry or slurry rheology.
Experience with materials sample preparation techniques, including milling, drying, pressing, and cross-sectioning.
High attention to detail and a methodical approach to measurement and data collection.
Demonstrated commitment to data quality, including careful documentation, verification, and review of results.
Ability to read, interpret, and implement standard operating procedures (SOPs) accurately.
Capability to contribute to the drafting and updating of SOPs based on laboratory experience and process improvements.
Knowledge of laboratory safety practices, including safe chemical handling, PPE requirements, and emergency procedures.
Ability to operate and maintain analytical instruments, perform routine calibrations, and troubleshoot basic equipment issues.
Strong organizational skills for maintaining inventory databases, calibration logs, and laboratory documentation.

Additional Skills & Qualifications

Academic or practical training in materials science, chemistry, chemical engineering, or a related discipline.
Experience working in a battery, energy storage, or advanced materials laboratory environment.
Familiarity with generating comparative datasets to support supplier qualification and material selection.
Experience writing clear technical reports, summary tables, and documentation for internal stakeholders.
Comfort working in a fast-paced, data-driven environment where analytical results inform purchasing and development decisions.

Work Environment

This role is fully onsite in a laboratory environment in San Leandro. You work primarily in a hands-on lab setting with analytical instruments such as particle size analyzers, BET surface area analyzers, XRD, SEM/EDS, TGA/DSC, rheometers, and conductivity measurement systems. Job Description

The Quality Control Lab Technician supports a high-volume manufacturing operation by performing accurate and timely quality testing on raw materials, bulk batches, and finished products. This role ensures that products meet strict specifications, communicates test results and batch adjustments clearly to production operators, and initiates investigations into non-conforming materials. The position offers strong long-term growth potential for someone who is proactive, detail-oriented, and eager to streamline testing processes and advance into higher-level technical roles over time.

Schedule: Thursday- Monday or Friday-Tuesday (8 am - 5 pm) or (7 am-4 pm)

Responsibilities

Execute and adhere to all environmental, health, and safety (EHS) requirements, maintaining a safe work environment and following internal safety rules and procedures, including wearing appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE).
Participate in the general housekeeping of the plant and laboratory areas to maintain a clean, organized, and compliant workspace.
Comply with all company policies, procedures, and quality standards in daily activities.
Perform timely and accurate chemical, physical, and visual testing on raw materials, bulk batches, and finished goods using standard test procedures.
Determine raw material adjustment amounts for bulk batches to ensure products meet required specifications.
Enter test results for raw materials, bulk batches, and finished goods into the ERP system (SAP) accurately and promptly.
Perform timely usage decisions (accept or reject) for raw materials, bulk batches, and finished goods in SAP based on test results and specifications.
Collect and store retain samples of raw materials, bulk batches, and finished products as required for traceability and future investigations.
Take immediate action on internal non-conformances by creating notifications in SAP and performing initial investigations in collaboration with production operators.
Support customer complaint investigations by reviewing batch records, analyzing retain samples, and contributing to root cause analysis and corrective actions.

Monitor and maintain laboratory inventory of reagents, consumables, and supplies to ensure consistent testing capability.
Review the daily production schedule and ensure that test equipment, reagents, and methods are prepared to efficiently test all scheduled batches.
Provide accurate documentation and visual quality control labels for materials and products that are acceptable, rejected, or on hold.
Issue, complete, maintain, and process all relevant paperwork and records related to testing, non-conformances, and quality documentation.
Participate in monthly meetings focused on quality, safety, housekeeping, and waste minimization, contributing ideas for continuous improvement.
Communicate all critical issues and problems concerning quality control test equipment, potential testing delays, and quality risks promptly to management.

Bachelor of Science degree in Chemical Engineering or Chemistry.

Hands-on experience performing chemical, physical, and visual testing in a laboratory or production support setting.
Proficiency with ERP systems, specifically SAP, including entering test results and making usage decisions.
Working knowledge of Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Teams, and Microsoft Outlook for data management, communication, and coordination.
Strong communication skills with the ability to communicate promptly and clearly, and to be proactive rather than reactive.
High attention to detail and accuracy in testing, documentation, and data entry.
Experience participating in audits and working within ISO or similar quality management environments.
Exposure to or experience with root cause analysis and corrective action processes, including updating documentation.
Familiarity with lean manufacturing concepts and continuous improvement practices.
Ability to manage time effectively and handle multiple tasks in a fast-paced lab and production environment.
Demonstrated ability to work both independently and under the direction of senior lab staff, such as senior lab technicians, lab supervisors, or technical leaders.
Strong sense of ownership and responsibility as a quality gatekeeper for production.

Additional Skills & Qualifications

Experience in aerospace, manufacturing, or consumer products industries, particularly in operations or production support roles.
Familiarity with GC-MS (Gas ChromatographyMass Spectrometry) or similar analytical instrumentation.
Exposure to Six Sigma or other structured problem-solving methodologies.
Experience working in a quality control laboratory that supports adhesives or chemical products.
Prior involvement in customer complaint investigations and non-conformance management.
Experience working in a lean manufacturing environment with a focus on waste minimization and process optimization.
Demonstrated ability to streamline testing processes and reduce redundancy in lab workflows.
Proven record of participating in continuous improvement initiatives, including documentation updates and process enhancements.
Strong professional attitude with a desire to learn, grow, and assume greater responsibility over time, including potential progression into senior or leadership roles.

Job Title: Sample Control Technician 3 / Lab Technician 2
Job Description

This role focuses on logging, tracking, and coordinating the receipt and shipment of samples into and out of the laboratory while ensuring accurate documentation and regulatory compliance. The Sample Control Technician prepares bottle kits for clients, maintains precise sample identification and routing, and supports smooth daily laboratory operations through careful handling, organization, and safety-conscious practices.

Responsibilities

Log and track the receipt and shipment of all samples into and out of the laboratory while verifying receipt of samples.
Receive and unload incoming samples or consignments in accordance with DOT regulations and verify each receipt against the Chain of Custody (COC), matching it to the corresponding quote and documenting discrepancies on a daily basis.
Review COCs to ensure they are accurate, complete, and correct, and actively seek resolution for any discrepancies or incomplete information.
Log samples into the Laboratory Management System daily, assign lot numbers for tracking purposes, and distribute associated paperwork to Project Managers.
Label and organize samples so they can be clearly identified by their assigned lot numbers and deliver them to the appropriate laboratories for analysis on a daily basis.
Prepare bottle kits daily to be shipped to clients for sample collection and return, following established procedures and complying with EPA and DOT requirements.
Forward samples to other laboratories as needed in accordance with DOT regulations when tests cannot be performed at the current location.
Dispose of spent samples, waste, and other potentially hazardous materials in accordance with established procedures and environmental guidelines.
Monitor freezer and cooler temperatures daily to confirm that readings remain within standard operating procedure (SOP) guidelines and document any deviations as required.
Clean and organize the department daily to promote a clean, safe work environment and ensure a smooth flow of daily operations.
Maintain and promote safety at all times by conducting all operations in a safe and environmentally compliant manner.
Stock supplies and maintain inventory on a daily basis to ensure adequate materials are available to perform tasks efficiently and appropriately.

Essential Skills

Strong verbal and written communication skills to interact clearly with internal teams and accurately document sample information.
High level of attention to detail to ensure precise logging, labeling, and tracking of samples and Chain of Custody documentation.
Effective problem-solving skills to identify and resolve discrepancies in documentation and sample handling.
Advanced ability to work independently and manage time efficiently in a fast-paced laboratory environment.
Advanced knowledge of laboratory and testing procedures relevant to sample control and handling.
Advanced ability to analyze data and accurately document and record results in laboratory systems.
High school diploma or GED required.
57 years of experience in a laboratory, sample control, or closely related environment.

Additional Skills & Qualifications

Associates degree in laboratory science or a related field is preferred.
Familiarity with Chain of Custody (COC) processes and documentation.
Experience working with Laboratory Management Systems for logging and tracking samples.
Knowledge of DOT regulations related to the shipment and handling of laboratory samples.
Understanding of EPA requirements related to sample collection, packaging, and transport.
Comfort working with standard operating procedures (SOPs) and adhering to strict regulatory and quality standards.

The role is based in a laboratory setting that handles a high volume of incoming and outgoing samples, requiring frequent interaction with freezers, coolers, and other temperature-controlled storage. The position involves daily monitoring of equipment, handling of potentially hazardous materials, and adherence to DOT, EPA, and internal SOP requirements.
